title: Dynamic error budget tranche allocator & initiative cadence
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: As Redwood scales, teams consume shared capacity and traditional static error budget allocations lead to frequent contention, fragmented rollouts, and manual reallocation during incidents. Problem: Without a cadence-driven allocator, PMs and SREs spend significant time negotiating budgets and manually adjusting SLO windows. Proposal summary: Implement a dynamic 'tranche' allocator that divides overall product-level error budget into time-boxed tranches (weekly or biweekly) and assigns tranche slices to initiatives based on priority, historical burn rate, and early-warning signals. The allocator ties into the Initiative Tracker (dashboard) and automatically suggests reassignments when a tranche hits predefined burn thresholds. Goals: 1) Reduce manual reallocation overhead by 70% for cross-team reliability changes. 2) Improve predictability of rollouts by aligning initiative cadence with tranche windows. 3) Surface proactive mitigation recommendations before customer-visible SLA violations. Scope: - Backend: tranche allocation service, APIs for PMs/ENG to request slices, webhook to rollout controller. - Console: tranche calendar UI, per-initiative budget view, burn forecast chart. - Telemetry: SLI burn forecast, tranche-level alerts, audit log for allocations/changes. Acceptance criteria: - Tranche allocator can create/adjust tranches programmatically via API. - Console shows active tranche calendar and per-initiative allocation. - Alerts trigger when tranche burn reaches 60%, 80%, 95% with suggested mitigations. - Demonstrated reduction in manual allocation tickets in a 6-week pilot with 3 teams. Non-goals: replacing SLO definition or per-service SLIs; this is an allocation layer that sits above existing SLOs. Links: Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/Reliability/Dynamic+Tranche+Allocator, Draft PRD: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBcExample, Design mockups: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/example-designs

next_steps: 1) Confirm region-aware modifier with SRE (owner: Priya) by 2025-02-28. 2) ENG to spike forecast engine and surface API contract (owner: Marco) by 2025-03-04. 3) Design to finalize tranche calendar UI and accessibility constraints (owner: Lena) by 2025-03-06. 4) Prepare pilot runbook, rollbacks, and communication template to customers and internal teams.
risks: - Incorrect forecast model could cause premature throttling of initiatives. - Audit log gaps may complicate postmortems. - Cross-region traffic shifts might concentrate burn unexpectedly. Mitigations: conservative default tranche sizes for first two pilots, manual override path, and canary rollout for allocator itself.
acceptance_criteria: - API: POST /tranches creates a tranche; GET returns current allocations. - UI: calendar shows tranches and clickable initiative cards. - Alerts: automatic suggestions when tranche burn hits 60/80/95%. - Pilot: 3 teams complete pilot with documented outcomes and at least one documented reallocation event handled automatically.
notes: This ticket feeds into the broader Reliability Initiative OKR: 'Improve incident lead time and reduce cross-team SLO disputes'. Expect coordination with PMs of Search, Chat, and Embeddings. Track costs of additional telemetry storage for forecast horizon; include in budget review.
audit_log_requirement: allocation_change: timestamp, actor, old_allocation, new_allocation, reason
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): API and forecast spike; Phase 2 (3 weeks): allocator service + console beta; Phase 3 (1 week): pilot, monitoring, and retro.
owner_rotation: Marco Liu -> Priya Nair (SRE) for pilot observability
